title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Municipal Services Office coordination
sections.summary: The Municipal Services Office is a targeted Government effort to coordinate municipal services and make public service more citizen-centric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Municipal Services Office (MSO) is one such targeted effort by the Government to coordinate and ensure smoother delivery of municipal services, as well as to make public service more citizen-centric.

sections.label: Healthcare professionals facing abuse
sections.summary: It is estimated that 70% of healthcare professionals here have faced physical abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: That they are the Davids against the Goliaths of this world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It is estimated that 70% of healthcare professionals here have faced physical abuse.

sections.label: Reported abuse cases in hospitals
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean said restructured hospitals had 31 reported cases in 2013 and 34 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In reply to my Parliamentary Question earlier, Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean has said that among the restructured hospitals, there were 31 reported cases in 2013 and 34 cases in 2014.

sections.label: Question on abuse of public officers
sections.summary: The Member asks whether abuse or harassment towards public officers, especially frontline staff, has risen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can the Minister let me know if there has, indeed, been a rise in occurrences of abuse or harassment towards public officers, especially frontline staff?

sections.label: Frontline public servants report rising abuse
sections.summary: Public servants feel verbal and physical abuse is rising, alongside outsourcing, privatisation of engineering units and changed Government functioning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I know of many public servants serving on the frontline, residents and friends alike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: They have felt that incidents of verbal and physical abuse towards them are on the rise and this is, indeed, worrying in spite of efforts to mitigate them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Among others are the increase in the outsourcing of engineering services over the years, the privatisation of Government engineering units into commercial entities and the change in the way the Government functions; moving away from paddling to steering, to borrow a boating analogy.

sections.label: Engineering inputs and unfilled jobs
sections.summary: Half the economy is estimated to rely on engineering inputs, and four of 2015's top 10 unfilled jobs were engineering related.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, it is estimated that half our economy relies on inputs from engineers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2015, among the top 10 jobs that went unfilled for six months, four were engineering related.

sections.label: Civil Service engineer pay and hiring
sections.summary: Speaker urges review of engineers' pay, career path and recognition, and asks DPM Teo about 1,000 new public sector engineering jobs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: You just need to have one failure to end up in jail.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is timely for our Government to relook into the pay, career path, jobscope and recognition of engineers in the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When asking for engineering-related tenders, instead of simply award to the lowest, the engineering innovation and local Singaporean Core workforce should carry much higher weightage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad when Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean recently announced that the Government is hiring 1,000 engineers for the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can Deputy Prime Minister Teo share with us which Ministries and Statutory Boards these 1,000 jobs come from?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Also, what kind of engineering jobs are these?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: What levels of the hierarchy are these jobs and what are the skills and experience required?

sections.label: Public sector talent investments
sections.summary: The passage asks what investments the public sector is making to attract, develop and retain these talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: What investments is the public sector making to attract, develop and retain these talents?

sections.label: Strategy Group under PMO
sections.summary: Last July, the Strategy Group was set up under the Prime Minister's Office.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Last July, we set up the Strategy Group under PMO.

sections.label: Reorganising four Statutory Boards
sections.summary: Four Statutory Boards are reorganised: SSG, WSG, IMDA and GovTech, with stated roles for skills, media and government technology.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: It has also coordinated the plans and programmes across Ministries to set out the policy agenda for this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This year, we are reorganising four Statutory Boards to deepen capabilities and better tackle emerging challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and Workforce Singapore (WSG) will support our citizens in acquiring useful skills to remain employable.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Info-Communications Media Development Authority (IMDA) will develop and regulate the converging info-communications and media sectors in a holistic way, while the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) will transform Government services using technology.

sections.label: Five agencies adopt competency framework
sections.summary: Five public agencies have adopted a service competency framework.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: For a start, five public agencies – CPF Board, HDB, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, National Environment Agency and National Library Board – have adopted this service competency framework.

sections.label: Abuse cases against public officers
sections.summary: In 2015, 437 hurt or verbal abuse cases against public officers were reported, 344 from Home Team agencies and 93 from others.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In 2015, there were 437 cases of hurt or verbal abuse against public officers that were reported to the Police.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As mentioned during the Ministry of Home Affair's COS debate, 344 of these were from the Home Team agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The remaining 93 were from other public agencies.

sections.label: Public Service hiring more engineers
sections.summary: The Public Service will employ an additional 1,000 engineers this year, growing its pool of some 7,700 engineers by more than 13%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: First, the Public Service will employ an additional 1,000 engineers this year, which will grow our current pool of some 7,700 engineers by more than 13%.

sections.label: Raising public sector engineer salaries
sections.summary: Salaries of public sector engineers will be raised to attract and retain engineering and ICT officers in the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Second, we will raise the salaries of our public sector engineers to attract and retain engineering and information and communications technology (ICT) officers in the Public Service.

sections.label: New starting salaries for engineers
sections.summary: Starting salaries will be set at $3,800 monthly for engineers and $4,000 for ICT, an average rise of about 20%, implemented from mid-2016.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Taking reference from the market starting salaries of good engineering graduates, we will set the salaries for good engineers joining the Public Service upon graduation starting from $3,800 per month and those in ICT starting from $4,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This means an increase in starting salaries, on average, of about 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Agencies will implement new starting salaries and make the necessary salary adjustments from the middle of 2016.

sections.label: Centres of Excellence for engineering
sections.summary: Three Centres of Excellence at JTC, DSTA and GovTech will support Government organisations, optimise engineering resources and invest in R&D.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: They will support other Government organisations, optimise scarce engineering resources and invest in R&D to build cutting-edge engineering expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We have established three such Centres of Excellence: (a) JTC: for infrastructure projects and facilities management services, and R&D in innovation, safety and construction productivity; (b) Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA): in the areas of sensors, robotics and the integration of command systems, to boost our Smart Nation efforts; and(c) GovTech: for the digital transformation of the public sector, including nurturing ICT officers, to improve the delivery of public services for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We are in the process of establishing other Centres of Excellence in geospatial information science and cybersecurity.

sections.label: Corruption cases at 30-year lows
sections.summary: The number of corruption cases registered for CPIB investigations is at 30-year lows.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The number of corruption cases registered for CPIB investigations is at 30-year lows.

sections.label: MAS probing banks over 1MDB
sections.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore is currently probing 40 banks operating here for possible money laundering offences linked to 1MDB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The 1 Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) is a case in point.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is currently probing into 40 banks operating here for possible money laundering offences linked to 1MDB.

sections.label: Prevention of Corruption Act jurisdiction
sections.summary: The Prevention of Corruption Act gives extraterritorial jurisdiction over Singapore Citizens' acts overseas, and MAS has a preventive regime of licensing, regulations and supervision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our Prevention of Corruption Act provides for extraterritorial jurisdiction, such that acts of Singapore Citizens, even if it is done overseas, will be dealt with in the same manner as if they were committed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MAS has put in place a robust preventive regime that combines tough licensing requirements, strict regulations and rigorous supervision.

sections.label: Law enforcement foreign engagement
sections.summary: Law enforcement agencies engage foreign counterparts and investigate money laundering and related offences when information suggests illicit proceeds flowed into or through Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our law enforcement agencies proactively engage their foreign counterparts and investigate both money laundering and related offences when there is sufficient information to suggest that illicit proceeds have flowed into or through Singapore.

sections.label: 2015 births highest in 13 years
sections.summary: SG50 feel-good factor and enhanced parental perks helped 2015 end with at least 33,793 new babies, the highest in 13 years, exceeding 2012's 33,238 births.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Thanks to the SG50 "rah rah" which brought on a feel-good factor, coupled with enhanced parental perks, 2015 ended with at least 33,793 new babies – the highest in 13 years!

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This even exceeded the 33,238 births in 2012, the auspicious Year of the Dragon.

sections.label: Singapore low total fertility rate
sections.summary: According to the United Nations, Singapore is one of the bottom 10 countries in terms of total fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to the United Nations, Singapore is one of the bottom 10 countries in terms of the total fertility rate (TFR).

sections.label: Developed countries fertility rates
sections.summary: France leads with a TFR of around two, and Ireland, Iceland and New Zealand have a TFR above 1.5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Amongst the developed countries, there are some that are not doing too badly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I understand France is leading the pack, with a TFR of around two; not quite the same as Sub-Saharan Africa but much better than us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The best performers, as I understand, are France with a TFR of 2; and Ireland, Iceland, New Zealand, all of whom have a TFR of above 1.5.

sections.label: Game plan for marriage parenthood
sections.summary: A question asks PMO to share its game plan for encouraging marriage and parenthood among Singaporeans without compromising career aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Given the challenges we face and the aspirations of young Singaporeans, could PMO share what is its "game plan" in encouraging marriage and parenthood amongst Singaporeans, while not compromising on their pursuit of career aspirations?

sections.label: Informal sources of labour
sections.summary: Asks whether informal sources of labour such as nannies and community volunteers could supplement infant and childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, and I have mentioned this before, could we organise and tap on "informal sources of labour", such as the nannies and volunteers within the community, to supplement infant and childcare centres?

sections.label: PMO study feasibility
sections.summary: Asks whether the PMO could study the idea's feasibility and share other solutions it is considering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As such, could PMO study the feasibility of such an idea and, at the same time, could PMO also share what other solutions it is considering?

sections.label: Infant and childcare capacity
sections.summary: Says capacity should match estates with many young couples, is unevenly distributed, and the Danish private child-minder model could be tried.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the Singapore context, the key may be to ensure there is enough infant and childcare capacity in the estates and towns with many young couples, building infrastructure ahead of demand, as it were.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While there may be sufficient childcare capacity nationwide, it is unevenly distributed, as has been discussed in the House this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is also scope to experiment with the Danish model of private child-minders in specific blocks, precincts or estates.

sections.label: Extended childcare leave increase
sections.summary: Asks whether the PMO would increase extended childcare leave and peg it to the child's age and number of children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As the Government advocates working adults to have a better work-life balance, will PMO consider increasing the amount of extended childcare leave and pegging the amount of extended childcare leave to not only the age of the child, but also the number of children one has?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With growing gender equality and the ability for women in Singapore to self-actualise through their careers, the perceived downsides to parenthood are immediate and quantifiable − time and effort to take care of one's children, potential impact on one's career, and that is not counting stretch marks and potential weight gain from pregnancy − while the benefits or joys of parenthood seem vague in comparison.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While the Government pushes out policies to help with the costs of raising children, if we look around us, even those who can afford to have children are not having children.

sections.label: HR processes for new mothers
sections.summary: Asks whether human resource processes can ensure proper communication with new mothers so they do not feel penalised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For instance, at the corporate level, while we acknowledge short-term changes in work arrangements due to maternity leave, can we ensure that our human resource processes are such that there is proper communication with new mothers so that they do not feel that they are penalised for having a baby.

sections.label: Self-help groups for parents
sections.summary: Asks whether resources can promote self-help groups for young parents, including breastfeeding, online resources, play groups and voluntary child-minding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we put in resources to promote self-help groups for young parents, from promoting breastfeeding to use of online resources to organise play groups and make possible voluntary child-minding arrangements for young children?

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood Packages funding
sections.summary: Since 2001, billions of dollars have been committed in Marriage and Parenthood Packages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since 2001, we have committed billions of dollars in our Marriage and Parenthood Packages.

sections.label: Paternity leave legislation welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker says it is time to stop making excuses and welcomes legislating two weeks' paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, perhaps it is time for us to stop making excuses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I welcome the legislating of the two weeks' paternity leave.

sections.label: Family-friendly facilities in commercial buildings
sections.summary: The speaker asks why baby rooms are built and proposes working with architects, BCA and developers and legislating family-friendly facilities in new commercial buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, why build the baby room in the first place?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We should work with the Institute of Architects, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA), the Real Estate Developers' Association of Singapore and even legislate requirements for new commercial buildings to provide family-friendly facilities in the same way we enforce barrier-free access.

sections.label: Single mothers and adoption framework
sections.summary: Single mothers received a boost, and the speaker echoes a call to strengthen the adoption framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Single mothers received a much welcome boost yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Their children deserve the same start as others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, echo the call by Mr Christopher de Souza to correspondingly strengthen our adoption framework to allow those conflicted about the future of their children to know that adoption into a caring family is an option.

sections.label: BTO flat waiting times
sections.summary: Many young couples prefer their own homes before marrying and having children, but average BTO waiting time is about four years, sometimes five.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many young couples whom I have spoken to prefer to have their own homes before they get married and have children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, the average waiting time for a Build-To-Order (BTO) HDB flat is about four years today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On some occasions, this may even stretch to five years.

sections.label: Flat waiting time and PPHS questions
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether waiting time can be cut for married couples and about interim rental flats, PPHS applications and available flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the waiting time for flats be reduced significantly for young couples who have registered their marriages?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Also, for couples who are still waiting for their flats to be ready, can they be offered an interim rental flat under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Since 2013, what is the average number of applications received from couples under PPHS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How many flats are currently available under PPHS?

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up obstacles
sections.summary: Some companies cite the tight labour market and weakening global economy as obstacles, and only 40% of fathers used one week paid paternity leave last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: But some companies are saying that the tight labour market and a weakening global economy might be obstacles during implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It was reported that only 40% of fathers used their one week paid paternity leave in Singapore last year.

sections.label: Balancing company needs and FWAs
sections.summary: A balance is needed between company needs and family-centric workplaces in a tight labour market, and a sectoral approach to flexible work arrangements could be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: And especially as hon Member Mr Thomas Chua has pointed out, we also need to balance between what the company needs and how they can put in place family-centric workplaces in a tight labour market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We can consider a sectoral approach to tackling structural differences in implementing flexible work arrangements (FWAs).

sections.label: SMEs and flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Small and medium enterprises find it very difficult to adopt flexible work arrangements because of their small workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) find it very difficult to adopt FWAs because of their small workforce.

sections.label: Government help with child-raising expenses
sections.summary: The Government has done well to help with child-raising expenses through initiatives such as the Child Development Account and this year's First Step Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I know, like my Parliamentary colleague Mr Yam, I have changed my fair share of diapers, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I feel that the Government has done well to help with child-raising expenses via initiatives, such as the Child Development Account (CDA) and this year's First Step Grant.

sections.label: Multiracial society and citizenship assimilation
sections.summary: Singapore must be a multiracial and multicultural society with each group retaining its identity while remaining cohesive, and NPTD could consider working with ICA on assimilation criteria before granting citizenship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore has been, and always must be, a multiracial and multicultural society, with each group retaining its own identity while remaining cohesive as One Singaporean People.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And also, would NPTD consider working with ICA to perhaps implement certain assimilation criteria before we grant Singaporean citizenship?

sections.label: Platforms for integration
sections.summary: Differences and lack of understanding cause friction, so sufficient platforms are needed to foster mutual understanding and integration, with three main platforms noted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Sometimes, the differences and lack of understanding of the different practices cause friction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is, therefore, a need to ensure that there are sufficient platforms to foster greater mutual understanding and promote integration across the different groups in our population, including citizens, new citizens and foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: As a first step, I think it is important to reflect on the contact points that assisted with integration previously and if they are still relevant or applicable to the different demographics today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note three main platforms for integration, through, namely, (a) the Ethnic Integration Policy in HDB estates; (b) education in schools; and (c) National Service.

sections.label: New citizens in private housing
sections.summary: New citizens and PRs choosing private housing may form enclaves by staying among their own community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, we see a fair share of new citizens and Permanent Residents (PRs) electing to live in private housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There may be a preference to stay amongst their own community and this leads to enclaves being formed.

sections.label: Urban infrastructure and integration
sections.summary: Urban infrastructure could create common touch-points of integration, and engagement with international school students could share local norms and values.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We should consider how we can develop our urban infrastructure to facilitate the common touch-points of integration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We may also wish to ensure regular engagement with students from international schools so that there are opportunities to share local norms and values.

sections.label: Overseas Singaporeans and integration update
sections.summary: More than 210,000 Singaporeans live, work or study overseas for extended periods, 30% more over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But please allow me to start by first giving an update on our efforts to keep in touch with Overseas Singaporeans, integrate new citizens and stay open as a society.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are now more than 210,000 Singaporeans living, working or studying overseas for extended periods of time.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is remarkable; 30% more over 10 years.

sections.label: Singapore Citizens by Descent babies
sections.summary: As more Singaporeans work and live abroad, such babies increased about 15% in 10 years, averaging around 1,200 annually from 2006 to 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As more Singaporeans work and live abroad, the number of such babies has increased by about 15% in the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From 2006 to 2010, the average number of "Singapore Citizens by Descent" was around 1,200 annually.

sections.label: Citizenships granted last year
sections.summary: Last year 20,815 Singapore Citizenships were granted, including 1,600, or 8%, Singapore Citizens by Descent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Last year, 20,815 Singapore Citizenships were granted, and this included 1,600 or 8% of those "Singapore Citizens by Descent".

sections.label: Disbursements and foreign workforce growth
sections.summary: Since 2009, $13 million went to over 660 projects for about 270 organisations, and foreign workforce growth slowed as the economy restructured.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since 2009, we have disbursed $13 million to over 660 projects to about 270 organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I want to thank the organisers and urge them to keep up their very good efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, instead of growing our population more quickly, we have decided to press on with the restructuring of our economy towards one that is less dependent on manpower for growth.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As a result, the growth of our foreign workforce has slowed considerably.

sections.label: Births and total fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore recorded nearly 34,000 Golden Jubilee babies and a 2015 total fertility rate of 1.24, slightly above the decade's first-half average of 1.22.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This was the second highest in more than a decade, only very slightly lower than the high of 24,037 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We welcomed nearly 34,000 Golden Jubilee babies, which was the highest in more than a decade, more than even the 2012 Year of the Dragon.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our TFR in 2015 was 1.24, slightly above the average TFR of 1.22 in the first half of the decade.

sections.label: BTO mortgage instalments
sections.summary: Most buyers of BTO flats in non-mature estates pay nothing out of pocket for their mortgage instalments.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The majority of those who purchase BTO flats in non-mature estates do not pay anything out of pocket for their mortgage instalments.

sections.label: BTO waiting times
sections.summary: Waiting times are currently about three to four years, depending on project design and site constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Waiting times are currently about three to four years, depending on the design and site constraints of the project.

sections.label: Resale flats and housing grants
sections.summary: With the new Proximity Housing Grant, couples buying a resale flat near their parents can get up to $90,000 in housing grants for their first home.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Resale flats are another option and, with the new Proximity Housing Grant for those buying a resale flat near their parents, couples can enjoy up to $90,000 in housing grants for their first home.

sections.label: Childcare places added
sections.summary: More than 30,000 childcare places have been added since 2013, most of them in HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: More than 30,000 childcare places have been added since 2013, most of which are in HDB estates.

sections.label: MediSave pre-delivery withdrawal limits
sections.summary: Minister Heng Swee Keat announced that MediSave withdrawal limits for pre-delivery costs will double from $450 to $900.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Minister Heng Swee Keat had announced earlier that we will double the MediSave withdrawal limits for pre-delivery costs from the current $450 to $900.

sections.label: South Korea fertility example
sections.summary: South Korea shows that government resources may not make couples want children or more children.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The example of South Korea suggests that even with abundant resources poured in by the Government, couples may still not want children or have more children.

sections.label: Absenteeism, motivation, productivity rates
sections.summary: The passage states 41% lower absenteeism, 32% higher motivation and 23% higher employee productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Forty-one percent lower absenteeism rates, 32% higher motivation rates and 23% higher employee productivity.

sections.label: Protection for pregnant women
sections.summary: In 2013, legal protection was enhanced for pregnant women against retrenchment or dismissal without sufficient cause.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2013, we enhanced legal protection for pregnant women against retrenchment or dismissal without sufficient cause.

sections.label: MOM Work-Life Grant
sections.summary: MOM offers the Work-Life Grant, providing up to $160,000 to support companies piloting, implementing and sustaining FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MOM offers businesses the Work-Life Grant, which provides up to $160,000 to support companies in piloting, implementing and sustaining FWAs.

sections.label: Breastfeeding rates and benefits
sections.summary: Dr Amy Khor spoke of breastfeeding health benefits, but a 2011 survey showed only 1% of mothers sustained exclusive breastfeeding to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Dr Amy Khor had spoken earlier about the health benefits of breastfeeding.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, a 2011 survey showed that only 1% of mothers in Singapore have been able to sustain exclusive breastfeeding to the six-month mark.

sections.label: Enhanced parental leave provisions
sections.summary: A second week of paternity leave is legislated for citizen fathers from 1 January 2017, and shared parental leave rises to four weeks from 1 July 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is in this spirit that I am announcing some enhancements to our parental leave provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will legislate a second week of paternity leave for all fathers of Singapore Citizens born from 1 January 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In addition, we will increase flexibility for couples in caring for their newborns by increasing shared parental leave from one week to four weeks for citizen children born from 1 July 2017.

sections.label: Adoption leave for adoptive parents
sections.summary: Adoption leave for adoptive mothers rises from four to 12 weeks for infants under one, and adoptive fathers may share four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To support couples who adopt, we will increase adoption leave for adoptive mothers, from the current four weeks, to 12 weeks for infants younger than one year old.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Adoptive fathers will also be able to share four weeks of their spouse's adoption leave.

sections.label: Funding paternity and parental leave
sections.summary: The Government will fully fund the enhancements to paternity and shared parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In addition, the Government will fully fund the enhancements to the paternity and shared parental leave.

sections.label: Community support for parenthood
sections.summary: Support for marriage and parenthood is enhanced through paternity leave and flexibility, but the whole community and employers must also support parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, we are enhancing our support to help Singaporeans fulfil their marriage and parenthood aspirations, by increasing paternity leave and offering more flexibility for fathers to share their wives' maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, it is clear that in order to make Singapore a "Great Place for Families", we cannot simply rely on Government policies alone.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We urgently need to mobilise the whole community, so that the entire society supports and celebrates parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We especially hope that more employers can recognise that it is in fact a wise move to help their employees take care of their family because this will not only increase productivity, but also help attract and retain talent.

sections.label: Sustainable population vision
sections.summary: The overall vision is a sustainable population enabling all citizens to enjoy a good standard of living now and in future.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our overall vision for Singapore is a sustainable population that enables all our citizens to enjoy a good standard of living, for this generation and long into the future.

sections.label: Public Service engineer recruitment
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister was asked about about 1,000 engineers the Public Service will employ and whether enough exist, with starting salaries up 20%.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister mentioned about 1,000 engineers that the Public Service sector is going to employ.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: And whether the Deputy Prime Minister thinks that there are sufficient engineers out there for the Public Service sector to recruit?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: It is good to note that the starting salary will be increased by 20%.

sections.label: Reviewing salaries throughout careers
sections.summary: Salaries will be reviewed not just at the starting level but throughout careers to ensure good progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: For salaries, we will review salaries not just at the starting level, but also throughout their careers to make sure that progression is good.

sections.label: 1MDB bank accounts frozen
sections.summary: In February, the Commercial Affairs Department and Monetary Authority of Singapore froze many bank accounts for suspected money laundering and other offences connected with 1MDB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Despite that, in February this year, our Commercial Affairs Department and the Monetary Authority of Singapore announced that they froze a large number of bank accounts for suspected money laundering and other offences connected with 1MDB.

sections.label: Combination of skills for companies
sections.summary: The speaker names Mr Koh Boon Hwee, Mr Liew Mun Leong and Mr Chew Choon Seng and says companies need a combination of technical, financial and marketing skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: People like Mr Koh Boon Hwee, Mr Liew Mun Leong who runs CapitaLand, Mr Chew Choon Seng who ran Singapore Airlines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I would say that we should have a good combination of people with technical skills as well as good financial and marketing skills to run companies in which technical knowledge, technical competence are an important part of making that company competitive.

sections.label: Engineers' numeracy and problem-solving
sections.summary: Engineers tend to be very numerate and bring that problem-solving quality to financial or technical problems faced in companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The advantage that engineers have is that they tend to be very numerate and are able to bring that quality of problem-solving to the problems that they are faced with in companies, whether it is the financial  or technical type of problems.

sections.label: Employing foreigners if needed
sections.summary: If there are not enough Singaporeans to do the job, foreigners will be employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: If we do not have enough Singaporeans to do the job, we will employ foreigners.

sections.label: French preschool model study
sections.summary: From age three, France's equivalent of the MOE cares for children placed there by parents, with preschool and a morning curriculum, and the French model should be studied carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From three years old onwards, the equivalent of the MOE in France cares for all children placed there by the parents.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From age three, four, five, six, it is preschool, and they have a curriculum in the morning and lunch is within the school environment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I would say that the French model is something that we ought to study very, very carefully, simply because it has allowed many more of their women to stay in the workforce.

sections.label: Model being studied carefully
sections.summary: It is a model that is being studied very carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Indeed, it is a model that we are studying very carefully.
